paper_title: Copper-catalyzed aerobic oxidation of primary alcohols to carboxylic acids†

questions.question: In this paper, what chemical entity is denoted by the label '1a'?
What is the identity/structure of product 2a formed from 1a in the study?
questions.ground_truth_answer: n‑Hexadecanoic acid (palmitic acid), depicted as n‑C15H31COOH (CH3(CH2)14COOH).

questions.question: Under the standard Conditions A used for the aerobic oxidation of 1a, what solvent was used and what were the catalyst loadings of Cu(NO3)2·3H2O and TEMPO?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Solvent: DCE (1,2‑dichloroethane). Catalyst loadings: Cu(NO3)2·3H2O 10 mol% and TEMPO 10 mol% (KHSO4 10 mol% as co‑catalyst; reaction run under O2 balloon).

questions.question: Referring to Table 1, which condition gave the higher NMR yield of carboxylic acid 2a: entry 1 (no additive) or entry 13 (KHSO4)?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Entry 13 with KHSO4 gave the higher yield: 100% NMR yield of 2a, whereas entry 1 (no additive) gave 0% NMR yield of 2a (instead 61% aldehyde 2a').
